question: Which state in India achieved a literacy rate of 99.30%, becoming fully literate as declared on International Literacy Day 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Himachal Pradesh was declared fully literate by its Chief Minister on International Literacy Day, achieving a 99.30% literacy rate, surpassing the national average of 95%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Himachal Pradesh became the fourth state, after Tripura, Mizoram, and Goa, to achieve full functional literacy.**
 
• Ladakh is the first fully literate Union Territory of India.
 
• India's national literacy rate rose from 74% in 2011 to 80.9% in 2023–24.
 
• The ULLAS Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram enrolled over 3 crore learners with a 90% success rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ULLAS Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram__

 __
 
• A national literacy initiative aimed at promoting education and increasing literacy across India with over 3 crore learners enrolled.
 
 
 
• International Literacy Day (ILD)__
 __
 
• Observed annually on September 8, ILD highlights the importance of literacy, with a focus on different themes, such as "Promoting Literacy in the Digital Era" in 2025.
 
 
 
• India's Literacy Growth__
 
 
• The literacy rate in India has risen significantly, from 74% in 2011 to 80.9% in 2023–24, showing continued progress in national education efforts.
